text:
alex: ran the KV-only quant bench this morning: FP8-KV vs INT8-KV vs AWQ-gptq mix on redwood-13b-serve.
alex: setup: seq=2048, batch=1, prefix_cache enabled, cold/warm run pairs (cold = new worker, warm = after 100 requests).
alex: command used:
```
run_bench --model redwood-13b --mode kv-only --quant fp8-kv --batch 1 --seq 2048 --warmups 100 --out fp8_kv_coldwarm.log
run_bench --model redwood-13b --mode kv-only --quant int8-kv --batch 1 --seq 2048 --warmups 100 --out int8_kv_coldwarm.log
```
jess: nice. paste the 95p latencies and mem deltas when you have them.
alex: raw summary (median / 95p lat, mem):
- FP8-KV: cold med 28ms, cold 95p 120ms, warm med 12ms, warm 95p 36ms, gpu mem 4.1GB
- INT8-KV: cold med 26ms, cold 95p 88ms, warm med 11ms, warm 95p 32ms, gpu mem 5.6GB
- AWQ-GPTQ hybrid (kv quant + block-gptq): cold med 30ms, cold 95p 140ms, warm med 13ms, warm 95p 45ms, gpu mem 3.9GB
prateek: interesting — FP8 lowers steady mem ~25% vs int8-kv (weird but consistent with kernel packing), but cold tail for FP8 is worse than int8 by ~35ms at 95p.
angela: do we have breakdown of what causes the cold tail? kernel compile, allocator jitter, or kv-dequant hotspot?
alex: profiler traces point to kernel select + first KV-dequant path. On cold FP8 we hit a fallback path to a wider kernel for some attn blocks (logs show "kernel: fp8_to_fp32_fallback at step 1").
alex: snippet from trace:
```
[0.002s] kernel_select: fp8-opt path
[0.010s] allocation: ok
[0.012s] attn_kv_dequant: fallback -> run_dequant_fp32_slow
[0.148s] enqueue token
```
jess: so warm path avoids fallback because cached kernel gets JITed and we stay on the fast kernel. That explains warm drop.
prateek: have we tried microbatching larger (batch=2/4) to amortize the dequant cost? Could be a quick mitigation for FP8 cold tails.
alex: ran quick microbatch sweep: batch=1 vs 4 on FP8-KV cold 95p: 120ms -> 76ms, warm 95p: 36ms -> 30ms. Memory rises slightly to 4.3GB.
angela: tradeoff acceptable for background workloads where latency SLOs are looser. For interactive we prefer consistent 95p under 80ms.
prateek: also tested pre-warming: spin a tiny pool that does 10 dummy prompts per new worker. With pre-warm the FP8 cold 95p drops to ~50ms (still above int8 88ms? wait that's lower). Need to re-evaluate baseline numbers.
alex: corrected: int8 cold 95p was 88ms, fp8 cold 95p after pre-warm becomes 52ms, so pre-warm wins.
jess: what's the accuracy delta on eval sets (LLM-eval and rerank)?
alex: accuracy diffs vs fp32 baseline on eval set (top-1 exact match percentages):
- FP8-KV: -0.6% absolute
- INT8-KV: -0.4% absolute
- AWQ-GPTQ hybrid: -0.9% absolute
jess: so FP8 slightly worse than int8 on accuracy there, but memory wins. AWQ has worst accuracy but best mem.
angela: for Dedicated customers with tight P50 P95 SLOs we should prefer INT8-KV as default for interactive. For background embeddings/rerank/offline jobs FP8 or AWQ is fine.
prateek: propose runtime policy: route requests with realtime=true -> int8-kv; realtime=false && priority<50 -> fp8-kv (or awq if mem constraint). Add pre-warm for new workers when route==int8-kv? maybe only for fp8.
jess: +1. Also create a canary that ramps FP8 on low-traffic region to verify real-world tails.
alex: will open a PR with configs and the bench artifacts: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/kv-quant/commit/3b9c8a
ci-bot: build passed for bench infra, artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/1794602222/
angela: next steps: 1) implement route policy (prateek) 2) add pre-warm hook for new workers (alex) 3) run 1-week canary with FP8 for background (jess) 4) update docs on console defaults (docs). assign owners?
prateek: taking #1, alex taking #2, jess taking #3, i'll ping docs for #4.
alex: ack. I'll paste the full logs to the PR and include the perf traces and flamegraphs.
jess: thanks — this is actionable. :thumbsup:
